analyst.summary: Kaynes had a strong FY26 on revenue (+33-34%) but profit growth lagged (PAT +24%, Q4 PAT actually down 21.5% YoY) as margins compressed and, more importantly, operating cash flow turned sharply negative (~-₹600cr) as receivables ballooned — customers are taking longer to pay even as the order book (~₹9,000cr) keeps growing. The balance sheet itself is not stressed (low debt, healthy current ratio), and the new government-backed semiconductor (OSAT) plant at Sanand just went into commercial production, which is a genuine long-term positive. But the stock still trades near 60x trailing earnings after already falling ~56% from its 52-week high on a guidance miss and two broker downgrades — the valuation still assumes a smooth, well-funded growth story that the FY26 cash-flow numbers have just called into question. We are holding, not adding, and watching the next 1-2 quarters' cash conversion closely before any change of view.
